rationale: Both score the game with the same frame-walking loop and both handle the tenth frame correctly. A keeps a hand-maintained state machine with frame, throwInFrame, tenthThrow, pinsLeft and over alongside the rolls slice. Some of that state overlaps (throwInFrame and tenthThrow count the same kind of thing in different frames), and the tenth-frame switch looks back into rolls by index. That is workable, but every update must keep all the fields consistent. B stores only the rolls and derives over() and pinsLeft() from them, so there is a single source of truth and the state cannot drift. It also declares its errors once as package-level sentinel values, which is idiomatic Go and lets callers compare errors. B's drawbacks are an O(n) rescan on each roll, which does not matter at this scale, a somewhat intricate over() and capitalised error strings. On balance its simpler data model and cleaner error handling make it slightly better.
